core_job: The user is someone furnishing or rearranging one real room with a tape measure. From a few measurements (the walls, the doors and windows, and the real sizes of the furniture), RoomCraft draws the room to scale, lays the pieces out by the rules for that room type, and gives a verdict: Fits, Tight or Doesn't work. Today the app is three disconnected text forms. Design prints furniture names. Redesign is a keyword match that the code still calls 'OCR', though nothing scans. Sourcing is a real OpenStreetMap shop search, but nothing connects it to the room the user planned. Baseline measured today: flutter analyze is clean and 96 tests pass.
signature: Clearance Check. Each room gets a list of checks. Each check shows the gap you have, the gap you need, and where the rule comes from. The rules are the clearance numbers already in room_type.dart (sofa to coffee table 14–18 in, 24 in beside the bed, 36 in in front of dressers, 42/48 in kitchen aisle, a 13–26 ft work triangle, 21 in clear in a bathroom), plus door swing, 12 in from a radiator and 30 in walkways. Failing gaps are hatched on the plan. Each failure gets a computed fix: the smallest move that works, or the largest piece size that passes, found by bisection (for example 'widest sofa that fits on this wall: 78 in'). Everything runs on the device. I checked five planner apps through the iTunes Search/Lookup API: Planner 5D (id606173978), Home Planner AI (id1076159017), 4Plan (id1570446253), magicplan (id427424432) and Will It Fit? AR (id6768062410). None of their full descriptions mentions clearance, walkway, door swing or spacing. That is a check of their descriptions only. WebSearch was disabled, so I could not test the apps themselves, and I did not verify IKEA's or Wayfair's planners.
must: M1 Core job: a 4-step New room flow (room type, width and length in ft+in or m+cm, doors and windows and fixed features placed on walls with the Notes field kept as a keyword helper, pieces at real sizes with every default labelled 'Typical — measure yours'). A to-scale CustomPainter plan with drag, 90° rotation and snapping, and a deterministic auto-layout. Remove every 'OCR' name and the document_scanner icon. A semantics summary for the canvas.

M2 Signature: Clearance Check. A typed rule table built from room_type.dart plus door swing, radiator, window and walkway checks. Each check shows the measured gap against the required gap, as pass, tight or fail, with hatched bands on the plan. Computed fixes: the smallest move, or the largest size that passes. A room verdict of Fits, Tight or Doesn't work. A unit test for every rule.

M3 Redesign mode: duplicates the room and re-lays out the user's own pieces. Shows before and after with failing-check counts. Optional style palette shown as real swatches, and suggested additions only where a passing spot exists. The source room is never changed.

M4 Materials and shops, limited to this room: paint, flooring, skirting and rug quantities computed from the room's geometry, with formulas and editable labelled assumptions. One Overpass query for only the shop types the room's list needs. Shop rows show OSM address, hours, phone and website where tagged, plus Directions and Save to room, and the ODbL attribution. No free-text material search (the NearServe boundary).

M5 Depth: rooms saved on the device as versioned JSON, with rename, duplicate and delete with undo. Filter by room type and verdict, and search by name. Share the plan as a PNG and the materials list as text. Real states for empty, no pieces, offline with Retry (Overpass failed once in today's curl), no shops and a corrupt file. Everything except the shop search works offline.

M6 Own identity: seed eucalyptus #35524A, tape-yellow accent #F2C230, tracing paper #EEF0EA with a #D5DBD0 grid, graphite ink #2D3033, brick #C8442B for clashes, plus a dark variant. None of these hexes appears anywhere else under /Users/spatchava/agl. Bundled Albert Sans for UI and Geist Mono for every measurement, both OFL, both curl 200, neither used by any other app or spec. Square-cornered hairline shapes. A Rooms home made of mini floor-plan cards under a large title, replacing the NavigationBar shell and the banner above it. A Plan · Check · Materials segmented editor that uses Cupertino widgets on iOS. The empty state is the onboarding. Its own Settings, with no AglLanguageScreen. New icon not from generate_app_icons.py, new splash (shasum must differ from 3f6a9b27d80d), display name and Android label 'RoomCraft'. Delete the duplicate crash_reporting.dart. Split main.dart into feature files.

M7 Honest under 5.6: every feature reachable on first launch with no account, demo data or seeded rooms. No feature-changing dart-defines. No region, date or reviewer detection beyond UMP. A test that greps lib/ and finds no Remote Config reads, plus a request to the package owner for AglInsights.init(remoteConfig: false). Every default labelled as an assumption. No prices, ratings or fake lists.

M8 Proven: analyze clean and more than the 96-test baseline. Coverage kept for accessibility, responsive, foldable, ads placement, privacy choices, i18n, release sanity and privacy manifest, with tests for removed UI rewritten rather than deleted. A new identity test. The screenshot integration test rewritten to drive the real UI. Built, launched and screenshotted on the simulator and emulator. Path-limited commits that never include fastlane/ or Podfile.lock, pushed to main.
